on {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:大年寺山]], which are known as the {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:大年寺山横穴墓群]]. Additionally, the {{ill|Futatsusawa Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:二ツ沢横穴墓群]], the {{ill|Mogasaki Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]], and the {{ill|Sōzenji Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:宗禅寺横穴墓群]] are found along the Hirose River, all collectively referred to as the {{ill|Mukaigaoka Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:向山横穴墓群]]. These tombs are believed to have been constructed from the late 7th century to the early 8th century. Approximately 2 kilometers southeast of this site is the {{ill|Kōriyama Ruins|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:郡山遺跡]], where the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:陸奥国]] was located at the time. It is speculated that these tombs were built by the people who lived in the capital and surrounding settlements.
{{right| [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9b.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Left-side cave]] [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9c.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Right-side cave (Photos taken in September 2006)]] ]]
In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a total of 34 tombs were found on the northern side of {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:大年寺山]] and on both the north and south slopes of Mount Atago. Additionally, it is reported that over ten more tombs were destroyed within the next few years. A map from the time shows three tombs on the northern slope of Atagoyama, three on the eastern slope, 20 on the southeastern slope, and nine other unidentified or destroyed tombs. The exact locations of the tombs recorded in this survey are now unknown, as many were lost due to residential development and road construction, making it impossible to determine their precise number and placement.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴). The accompanying map was hand-drawn and does not accurately reflect the modern altered landscape. The text states that 34 tombs exist, but only 33 are depicted with slanted lines, while other types of tombs or destroyed tombs are shown without explanation.</ref>
Since [[1973]] (Shōwa 48), surveys have focused on the tombs on the southern slope, where 28 tombs have been confirmed. In addition, a single horizontal tomb with red murals was found near the southeastern slope. No excavations have been conducted on the northern side.
These tombs were built into the middle of the slopes, with a passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:羨道]]) approximately 1 meter wide leading to a slightly narrower entrance ({{ill|genmon|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:玄門]]), which then opens into the burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:玄室]]). Some tombs lack an entrance door. The length of the passage is unknown. The burial chambers are either rectangular or trapezoidal, sometimes with rounded corners, and most range from 1 to 3 meters per side. One tomb was found with stones laid over half of its floor.
Due to poor preservation conditions, the full range of burial goods is unclear. However, artifacts such as iron swords, iron arrowheads, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]], {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:土師器]], and {{ill|glass beads|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:ガラス玉]] have been found.
== Atagoyama Decorated Yokonahaka Burial Mound ==
Near the open tombs, a decorated horizontal tomb was discovered underground. The entrance passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:羨道]]) was 2.5 meters long and 1.15 meters wide at the bottom. The burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:玄室]]) was nearly square, measuring 1.8 meters (front), 1.9 meters (back), 1.8 meters (right), and 1.65 meters (left). The chamber is estimated to be about 1.4 meters high and shaped like either a house or a dome. The entrance appears to have been sealed with stacked stones, possibly with a door that has since disappeared. The construction of this tomb follows the same pattern as the others in the group.
The back wall of the burial chamber features decorations painted in red pigment, consisting of multiple circular and cross-shaped motifs arranged in a scattered pattern. Grave goods found in this tomb included one {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:土師器]] vessel, one small knife, the remains of five individuals, as well as unidentified iron objects, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]], and {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:土師器]] fragments.
This decorated tomb is estimated to date to the mid-to-late 7th century. The presence of murals suggests that a high-ranking individual may have been buried here. == Excavation History ==
The open cave tombs of {{ill|Mount Atago (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:愛宕山 (仙台市)]] have been known locally for a long time. A map published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1) records those on the northern side as {{ill|Emishi caves|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:蝦夷穴]].<ref>『最新版仙台全図』（『100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩』60頁）。</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), during road construction that cut into the mountain, numerous horizontal tombs were discovered, along with human remains, straight swords, and {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]]. However, all of these finds were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), p. 73.</ref>
The first systematic investigation of Atagoyama’s cave tombs was conducted by {{ill|Shimizu Toshiro|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:清水東四郎]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), when he reported a total of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), pp. 27–28.</ref> Later, {{ill|Ito Nobuo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:伊東信雄]] also took measurements of one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), pp. 72–73. The exact date of this survey is not mentioned in the text and may have been postwar.</ref>
During World War II, the open tombs were repurposed as air-raid shelters, and after the war, some were used as household storage spaces. As Sendai expanded, urban development destroyed additional tombs.
When {{ill|Atago Bridge (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:愛宕大橋]] was constructed, its connecting roads cut into the mountain's edge, prompting an official excavation by the Sendai City authorities. In [[1973]], ten cave tombs were confirmed on the southern slope, and nine of them were excavated. During this survey, a single {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]] vessel and human bones were discovered.<ref>『仙台市向山愛宕山横穴群発掘調査報告書』。</ref>
On April 21, [[1976]] (Shōwa 51), roadwork near the southeastern slope suddenly revealed a tomb containing human bones. The {{ill|Sendai South Police Station|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:仙台南警察署]] was notified and determined that the remains were ancient, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. This tomb turned out to be the decorated horizontal burial mound, the most significant discovery among the Atagoyama tombs. Although the chamber’s wall paintings were recognized as an important find, there were no resources for preservation at the time, and the tomb was reburied after documentation.<ref>『宮城県仙台市愛宕山装飾横穴古墳発掘調査報告書』。</ref> The site is located just outside the curve of {{ill|Hirosegawa Riverside Road|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:広瀬河畔通り]].
In September and October of [[1991]] (Heisei 3), an excavation was conducted before the construction of new housing. This revealed 18 underground cave tombs, of which 15 were investigated. Many of these had been partially damaged before the excavation, but artifacts such as straight swords and glass beads were still recovered.<ref>『仙台市愛宕山横穴墓群 第3次発掘調査報告書』。</ref>

== Excavation History == The existence of open tombs in Atagoyama was well known locally, and they were marked as "[[Emishi Caves]]" (蝦夷穴) on maps published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1).<ref>"Latest Sendai City Map" (最新版仙台全図) in *100 Years Ago in Sendai: Sendai Map Walk* (100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩), p. 60.</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), road construction led to the discovery of numerous horizontal tombs, along with human remains, straight swords, and Sue ware. However, these artifacts were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," p. 73.</ref>
The first formal survey of Atagoyama's tombs was conducted by [[Shimizu Toshiro]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), who reported the existence of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," pp. 27-28.</ref> Later, [[Ito Nobuo]] also measured one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," pp. 72-73.</ref>
During [[World War II]], some of the open tombs were used as air-raid shelters and later repurposed as storage spaces for private homes. As Sendai expanded post-war, residential developments destroyed several tombs.
During the construction of [[Atago Bridge]], road construction along the mountainside led to an investigation by Sendai City. In [[1973]], ten tombs on the southern slope were identified, with nine of them excavated. This excavation yielded a single Sue ware vessel and human remains.<ref>*Sendai City Mukaigaoka Atagoyama Yokonahaka Group Excavation Report*</ref>
In [[1991]], a pre-construction excavation for residential development uncovered 18 underground tombs, of which 15 were surveyed. Many had been partially destroyed, but some yielded straight swords and glass beads.<ref>*Sendai City Atagoyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group: Third Excavation Report*</ref>

on {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:大年寺山]], which are known as the {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:大年寺山横穴墓群]]. Additionally, the {{ill|Futatsusawa Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:二ツ沢横穴墓群]], the {{ill|Mogasaki Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]], and the {{ill|Sōzenji Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:宗禅寺横穴墓群]] are found along the Hirose River, all collectively referred to as the {{ill|Mukaigaoka Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:向山横穴墓群]]. These tombs are believed to have been constructed from the late 7th century to the early 8th century. Approximately 2 kilometers southeast of this site is the {{ill|Kōriyama Ruins|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:郡山遺跡]], where the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:陸奥国]] was located at the time. It is speculated that these tombs were built by the people who lived in the capital and surrounding settlements.
{{right| [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9b.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Left-side cave]] [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9c.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Right-side cave (Photos taken in September 2006)]] ]]
In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a total of 34 tombs were found on the northern side of {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:大年寺山]] and on both the north and south slopes of Mount Atago. Additionally, it is reported that over ten more tombs were destroyed within the next few years. A map from the time shows three tombs on the northern slope of Atagoyama, three on the eastern slope, 20 on the southeastern slope, and nine other unidentified or destroyed tombs. The exact locations of the tombs recorded in this survey are now unknown, as many were lost due to residential development and road construction, making it impossible to determine their precise number and placement.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴). The accompanying map was hand-drawn and does not accurately reflect the modern altered landscape. The text states that 34 tombs exist, but only 33 are depicted with slanted lines, while other types of tombs or destroyed tombs are shown without explanation.</ref>
Since [[1973]] (Shōwa 48), surveys have focused on the tombs on the southern slope, where 28 tombs have been confirmed. In addition, a single horizontal tomb with red murals was found near the southeastern slope. No excavations have been conducted on the northern side.
These tombs were built into the middle of the slopes, with a passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:羨道]]) approximately 1 meter wide leading to a slightly narrower entrance ({{ill|genmon|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:玄門]]), which then opens into the burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:玄室]]). Some tombs lack an entrance door. The length of the passage is unknown. The burial chambers are either rectangular or trapezoidal, sometimes with rounded corners, and most range from 1 to 3 meters per side. One tomb was found with stones laid over half of its floor.
Due to poor preservation conditions, the full range of burial goods is unclear. However, artifacts such as iron swords, iron arrowheads, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]], {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:土師器]], and {{ill|glass beads|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:ガラス玉]] have been found.
== Atagoyama Decorated Yokonahaka Burial Mound ==
Near the open tombs, a decorated horizontal tomb was discovered underground. The entrance passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:羨道]]) was 2.5 meters long and 1.15 meters wide at the bottom. The burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:玄室]]) was nearly square, measuring 1.8 meters (front), 1.9 meters (back), 1.8 meters (right), and 1.65 meters (left). The chamber is estimated to be about 1.4 meters high and shaped like either a house or a dome. The entrance appears to have been sealed with stacked stones, possibly with a door that has since disappeared. The construction of this tomb follows the same pattern as the others in the group.
The back wall of the burial chamber features decorations painted in red pigment, consisting of multiple circular and cross-shaped motifs arranged in a scattered pattern. Grave goods found in this tomb included one {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:土師器]] vessel, one small knife, the remains of five individuals, as well as unidentified iron objects, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]], and {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:土師器]] fragments.
This decorated tomb is estimated to date to the mid-to-late 7th century. The presence of murals suggests that a high-ranking individual may have been buried here. == Excavation History ==
The open cave tombs of {{ill|Mount Atago (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:愛宕山 (仙台市)]] have been known locally for a long time. A map published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1) records those on the northern side as {{ill|Emishi caves|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:蝦夷穴]].<ref>『最新版仙台全図』（『100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩』60頁）。</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), during road construction that cut into the mountain, numerous horizontal tombs were discovered, along with human remains, straight swords, and {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]]. However, all of these finds were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), p. 73.</ref>
The first systematic investigation of Atagoyama’s cave tombs was conducted by {{ill|Shimizu Toshiro|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:清水東四郎]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), when he reported a total of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), pp. 27–28.</ref> Later, {{ill|Ito Nobuo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:伊東信雄]] also took measurements of one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), pp. 72–73. The exact date of this survey is not mentioned in the text and may have been postwar.</ref>
During World War II, the open tombs were repurposed as air-raid shelters, and after the war, some were used as household storage spaces. As Sendai expanded, urban development destroyed additional tombs.
When {{ill|Atago Bridge (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:愛宕大橋]] was constructed, its connecting roads cut into the mountain's edge, prompting an official excavation by the Sendai City authorities. In [[1973]], ten cave tombs were confirmed on the southern slope, and nine of them were excavated. During this survey, a single {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]] vessel and human bones were discovered.<ref>『仙台市向山愛宕山横穴群発掘調査報告書』。</ref>
On April 21, [[1976]] (Shōwa 51), roadwork near the southeastern slope suddenly revealed a tomb containing human bones. The {{ill|Sendai South Police Station|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:仙台南警察署]] was notified and determined that the remains were ancient, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. This tomb turned out to be the decorated horizontal burial mound, the most significant discovery among the Atagoyama tombs. Although the chamber’s wall paintings were recognized as an important find, there were no resources for preservation at the time, and the tomb was reburied after documentation.<ref>『宮城県仙台市愛宕山装飾横穴古墳発掘調査報告書』。</ref> The site is located just outside the curve of {{ill|Hirosegawa Riverside Road|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:広瀬河畔通り]].
In September and October of [[1991]] (Heisei 3), an excavation was conducted before the construction of new housing. This revealed 18 underground cave tombs, of which 15 were investigated. Many of these had been partially damaged before the excavation, but artifacts such as straight swords and glass beads were still recovered.<ref>『仙台市愛宕山横穴墓群 第3次発掘調査報告書』。</ref>

== Excavation History == The existence of open tombs in Atagoyama was well known locally, and they were marked as "[[Emishi Caves]]" (蝦夷穴) on maps published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1).<ref>"Latest Sendai City Map" (最新版仙台全図) in *100 Years Ago in Sendai: Sendai Map Walk* (100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩), p. 60.</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), road construction led to the discovery of numerous horizontal tombs, along with human remains, straight swords, and Sue ware. However, these artifacts were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," p. 73.</ref>
The first formal survey of Atagoyama's tombs was conducted by [[Shimizu Toshiro]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), who reported the existence of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," pp. 27-28.</ref> Later, [[Ito Nobuo]] also measured one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," pp. 72-73.</ref>
During [[World War II]], some of the open tombs were used as air-raid shelters and later repurposed as storage spaces for private homes. As Sendai expanded post-war, residential developments destroyed several tombs.
During the construction of [[Atago Bridge]], road construction along the mountainside led to an investigation by Sendai City. In [[1973]], ten tombs on the southern slope were identified, with nine of them excavated. This excavation yielded a single Sue ware vessel and human remains.<ref>*Sendai City Mukaigaoka Atagoyama Yokonahaka Group Excavation Report*</ref>
In [[1991]], a pre-construction excavation for residential development uncovered 18 underground tombs, of which 15 were surveyed. Many had been partially destroyed, but some yielded straight swords and glass beads.<ref>*Sendai City Atagoyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group: Third Excavation Report*</ref>

on {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:大年寺山]], which are known as the {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:大年寺山横穴墓群]]. Additionally, the {{ill|Futatsusawa Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:二ツ沢横穴墓群]], the {{ill|Mogasaki Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]], and the {{ill|Sōzenji Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:宗禅寺横穴墓群]] are found along the Hirose River, all collectively referred to as the {{ill|Mukaigaoka Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:向山横穴墓群]]. These tombs are believed to have been constructed from the late 7th century to the early 8th century. Approximately 2 kilometers southeast of this site is the {{ill|Kōriyama Ruins|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:郡山遺跡]], where the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:陸奥国]] was located at the time. It is speculated that these tombs were built by the people who lived in the capital and surrounding settlements.
{{right| [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9b.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Left-side cave]] [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9c.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Right-side cave (Photos taken in September 2006)]] ]]
In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a total of 34 tombs were found on the northern side of {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:大年寺山]] and on both the north and south slopes of Mount Atago. Additionally, it is reported that over ten more tombs were destroyed within the next few years. A map from the time shows three tombs on the northern slope of Atagoyama, three on the eastern slope, 20 on the southeastern slope, and nine other unidentified or destroyed tombs. The exact locations of the tombs recorded in this survey are now unknown, as many were lost due to residential development and road construction, making it impossible to determine their precise number and placement.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴). The accompanying map was hand-drawn and does not accurately reflect the modern altered landscape. The text states that 34 tombs exist, but only 33 are depicted with slanted lines, while other types of tombs or destroyed tombs are shown without explanation.</ref>
Since [[1973]] (Shōwa 48), surveys have focused on the tombs on the southern slope, where 28 tombs have been confirmed. In addition, a single horizontal tomb with red murals was found near the southeastern slope. No excavations have been conducted on the northern side.
These tombs were built into the middle of the slopes, with a passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:羨道]]) approximately 1 meter wide leading to a slightly narrower entrance ({{ill|genmon|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:玄門]]), which then opens into the burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:玄室]]). Some tombs lack an entrance door. The length of the passage is unknown. The burial chambers are either rectangular or trapezoidal, sometimes with rounded corners, and most range from 1 to 3 meters per side. One tomb was found with stones laid over half of its floor.
Due to poor preservation conditions, the full range of burial goods is unclear. However, artifacts such as iron swords, iron arrowheads, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]], {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:土師器]], and {{ill|glass beads|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:ガラス玉]] have been found.
== Atagoyama Decorated Yokonahaka Burial Mound ==
Near the open tombs, a decorated horizontal tomb was discovered underground. The entrance passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:羨道]]) was 2.5 meters long and 1.15 meters wide at the bottom. The burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:玄室]]) was nearly square, measuring 1.8 meters (front), 1.9 meters (back), 1.8 meters (right), and 1.65 meters (left). The chamber is estimated to be about 1.4 meters high and shaped like either a house or a dome. The entrance appears to have been sealed with stacked stones, possibly with a door that has since disappeared. The construction of this tomb follows the same pattern as the others in the group.
The back wall of the burial chamber features decorations painted in red pigment, consisting of multiple circular and cross-shaped motifs arranged in a scattered pattern. Grave goods found in this tomb included one {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:土師器]] vessel, one small knife, the remains of five individuals, as well as unidentified iron objects, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]], and {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:土師器]] fragments.
This decorated tomb is estimated to date to the mid-to-late 7th century. The presence of murals suggests that a high-ranking individual may have been buried here. == Excavation History ==
The open cave tombs of {{ill|Mount Atago (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:愛宕山 (仙台市)]] have been known locally for a long time. A map published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1) records those on the northern side as {{ill|Emishi caves|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:蝦夷穴]].<ref>『最新版仙台全図』（『100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩』60頁）。</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), during road construction that cut into the mountain, numerous horizontal tombs were discovered, along with human remains, straight swords, and {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]]. However, all of these finds were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), p. 73.</ref>
The first systematic investigation of Atagoyama’s cave tombs was conducted by {{ill|Shimizu Toshiro|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:清水東四郎]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), when he reported a total of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), pp. 27–28.</ref> Later, {{ill|Ito Nobuo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:伊東信雄]] also took measurements of one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), pp. 72–73. The exact date of this survey is not mentioned in the text and may have been postwar.</ref>
During World War II, the open tombs were repurposed as air-raid shelters, and after the war, some were used as household storage spaces. As Sendai expanded, urban development destroyed additional tombs.
When {{ill|Atago Bridge (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:愛宕大橋]] was constructed, its connecting roads cut into the mountain's edge, prompting an official excavation by the Sendai City authorities. In [[1973]], ten cave tombs were confirmed on the southern slope, and nine of them were excavated. During this survey, a single {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:須恵器]] vessel and human bones were discovered.<ref>『仙台市向山愛宕山横穴群発掘調査報告書』。</ref>
On April 21, [[1976]] (Shōwa 51), roadwork near the southeastern slope suddenly revealed a tomb containing human bones. The {{ill|Sendai South Police Station|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:仙台南警察署]] was notified and determined that the remains were ancient, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. This tomb turned out to be the decorated horizontal burial mound, the most significant discovery among the Atagoyama tombs. Although the chamber’s wall paintings were recognized as an important find, there were no resources for preservation at the time, and the tomb was reburied after documentation.<ref>『宮城県仙台市愛宕山装飾横穴古墳発掘調査報告書』。</ref> The site is located just outside the curve of {{ill|Hirosegawa Riverside Road|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[ja:広瀬河畔通り]].
In September and October of [[1991]] (Heisei 3), an excavation was conducted before the construction of new housing. This revealed 18 underground cave tombs, of which 15 were investigated. Many of these had been partially damaged before the excavation, but artifacts such as straight swords and glass beads were still recovered.<ref>『仙台市愛宕山横穴墓群 第3次発掘調査報告書』。</ref>

== Excavation History == The existence of open tombs in Atagoyama was well known locally, and they were marked as "[[Emishi Caves]]" (蝦夷穴) on maps published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1).<ref>"Latest Sendai City Map" (最新版仙台全図) in *100 Years Ago in Sendai: Sendai Map Walk* (100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩), p. 60.</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), road construction led to the discovery of numerous horizontal tombs, along with human remains, straight swords, and Sue ware. However, these artifacts were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," p. 73.</ref>
The first formal survey of Atagoyama's tombs was conducted by [[Shimizu Toshiro]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), who reported the existence of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," pp. 27-28.</ref> Later, [[Ito Nobuo]] also measured one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," pp. 72-73.</ref>
During [[World War II]], some of the open tombs were used as air-raid shelters and later repurposed as storage spaces for private homes. As Sendai expanded post-war, residential developments destroyed several tombs.
During the construction of [[Atago Bridge]], road construction along the mountainside led to an investigation by Sendai City. In [[1973]], ten tombs on the southern slope were identified, with nine of them excavated. This excavation yielded a single Sue ware vessel and human remains.<ref>*Sendai City Mukaigaoka Atagoyama Yokonahaka Group Excavation Report*</ref>
In [[1991]], a pre-construction excavation for residential development uncovered 18 underground tombs, of which 15 were surveyed. Many had been partially destroyed, but some yielded straight swords and glass beads.<ref>*Sendai City Atagoyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group: Third Excavation Report*</ref>

on {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山]], which are known as the {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山横穴墓群]]. Additionally, the {{ill|Futatsusawa Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:二ツ沢横穴墓群]], the {{ill|Mogasaki Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]], and the {{ill|Sōzenji Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:宗禅寺横穴墓群]] are found along the Hirose River, all collectively referred to as the {{ill|Mukaigaoka Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:向山横穴墓群]]. These tombs are believed to have been constructed from the late 7th century to the early 8th century. Approximately 2 kilometers southeast of this site is the {{ill|Kōriyama Ruins|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:郡山遺跡]], where the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:陸奥国]] was located at the time. It is speculated that these tombs were built by the people who lived in the capital and surrounding settlements.
{{right| [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9b.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Left-side cave]] [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9c.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Right-side cave (Photos taken in September 2006)]] ]]
In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a total of 34 tombs were found on the northern side of {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山]] and on both the north and south slopes of Mount Atago. Additionally, it is reported that over ten more tombs were destroyed within the next few years. A map from the time shows three tombs on the northern slope of Atagoyama, three on the eastern slope, 20 on the southeastern slope, and nine other unidentified or destroyed tombs. The exact locations of the tombs recorded in this survey are now unknown, as many were lost due to residential development and road construction, making it impossible to determine their precise number and placement.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴). The accompanying map was hand-drawn and does not accurately reflect the modern altered landscape. The text states that 34 tombs exist, but only 33 are depicted with slanted lines, while other types of tombs or destroyed tombs are shown without explanation.</ref>
Since [[1973]] (Shōwa 48), surveys have focused on the tombs on the southern slope, where 28 tombs have been confirmed. In addition, a single horizontal tomb with red murals was found near the southeastern slope. No excavations have been conducted on the northern side.
These tombs were built into the middle of the slopes, with a passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:羨道]]) approximately 1 meter wide leading to a slightly narrower entrance ({{ill|genmon|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄門]]), which then opens into the burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄室]]). Some tombs lack an entrance door. The length of the passage is unknown. The burial chambers are either rectangular or trapezoidal, sometimes with rounded corners, and most range from 1 to 3 meters per side. One tomb was found with stones laid over half of its floor.
Due to poor preservation conditions, the full range of burial goods is unclear. However, artifacts such as iron swords, iron arrowheads, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]], {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]], and {{ill|glass beads|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:ガラス玉]] have been found.
== Atagoyama Decorated Yokonahaka Burial Mound ==
Near the open tombs, a decorated horizontal tomb was discovered underground. The entrance passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:羨道]]) was 2.5 meters long and 1.15 meters wide at the bottom. The burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄室]]) was nearly square, measuring 1.8 meters (front), 1.9 meters (back), 1.8 meters (right), and 1.65 meters (left). The chamber is estimated to be about 1.4 meters high and shaped like either a house or a dome. The entrance appears to have been sealed with stacked stones, possibly with a door that has since disappeared. The construction of this tomb follows the same pattern as the others in the group.
The back wall of the burial chamber features decorations painted in red pigment, consisting of multiple circular and cross-shaped motifs arranged in a scattered pattern. Grave goods found in this tomb included one {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]] vessel, one small knife, the remains of five individuals, as well as unidentified iron objects, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]], and {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]] fragments.
This decorated tomb is estimated to date to the mid-to-late 7th century. The presence of murals suggests that a high-ranking individual may have been buried here. == Excavation History ==
The open cave tombs of {{ill|Mount Atago (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:愛宕山 (仙台市)]] have been known locally for a long time. A map published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1) records those on the northern side as {{ill|Emishi caves|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:蝦夷穴]].<ref>『最新版仙台全図』（『100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩』60頁）。</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), during road construction that cut into the mountain, numerous horizontal tombs were discovered, along with human remains, straight swords, and {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]]. However, all of these finds were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), p. 73.</ref>
The first systematic investigation of Atagoyama’s cave tombs was conducted by {{ill|Shimizu Toshiro|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:清水東四郎]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), when he reported a total of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), pp. 27–28.</ref> Later, {{ill|Ito Nobuo|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:伊東信雄]] also took measurements of one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), pp. 72–73. The exact date of this survey is not mentioned in the text and may have been postwar.</ref>
During World War II, the open tombs were repurposed as air-raid shelters, and after the war, some were used as household storage spaces. As Sendai expanded, urban development destroyed additional tombs.
When {{ill|Atago Bridge (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:愛宕大橋]] was constructed, its connecting roads cut into the mountain's edge, prompting an official excavation by the Sendai City authorities. In [[1973]], ten cave tombs were confirmed on the southern slope, and nine of them were excavated. During this survey, a single {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]] vessel and human bones were discovered.<ref>『仙台市向山愛宕山横穴群発掘調査報告書』。</ref>
On April 21, [[1976]] (Shōwa 51), roadwork near the southeastern slope suddenly revealed a tomb containing human bones. The {{ill|Sendai South Police Station|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:仙台南警察署]] was notified and determined that the remains were ancient, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. This tomb turned out to be the decorated horizontal burial mound, the most significant discovery among the Atagoyama tombs. Although the chamber’s wall paintings were recognized as an important find, there were no resources for preservation at the time, and the tomb was reburied after documentation.<ref>『宮城県仙台市愛宕山装飾横穴古墳発掘調査報告書』。</ref> The site is located just outside the curve of {{ill|Hirosegawa Riverside Road|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:広瀬河畔通り]].
In September and October of [[1991]] (Heisei 3), an excavation was conducted before the construction of new housing. This revealed 18 underground cave tombs, of which 15 were investigated. Many of these had been partially damaged before the excavation, but artifacts such as straight swords and glass beads were still recovered.<ref>『仙台市愛宕山横穴墓群 第3次発掘調査報告書』。</ref>

== Excavation History == The existence of open tombs in Atagoyama was well known locally, and they were marked as "[[Emishi Caves]]" (蝦夷穴) on maps published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1).<ref>"Latest Sendai City Map" (最新版仙台全図) in *100 Years Ago in Sendai: Sendai Map Walk* (100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩), p. 60.</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), road construction led to the discovery of numerous horizontal tombs, along with human remains, straight swords, and Sue ware. However, these artifacts were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," p. 73.</ref>
The first formal survey of Atagoyama's tombs was conducted by [[Shimizu Toshiro]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), who reported the existence of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," pp. 27-28.</ref> Later, [[Ito Nobuo]] also measured one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," pp. 72-73.</ref>
During [[World War II]], some of the open tombs were used as air-raid shelters and later repurposed as storage spaces for private homes. As Sendai expanded post-war, residential developments destroyed several tombs.
During the construction of [[Atago Bridge]], road construction along the mountainside led to an investigation by Sendai City. In [[1973]], ten tombs on the southern slope were identified, with nine of them excavated. This excavation yielded a single Sue ware vessel and human remains.<ref>*Sendai City Mukaigaoka Atagoyama Yokonahaka Group Excavation Report*</ref>
In [[1991]], a pre-construction excavation for residential development uncovered 18 underground tombs, of which 15 were surveyed. Many had been partially destroyed, but some yielded straight swords and glass beads.<ref>*Sendai City Atagoyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group: Third Excavation Report*</ref>

on {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山]], which are known as the {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山横穴墓群]]. Additionally, the {{ill|Futatsusawa Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:二ツ沢横穴墓群]], the {{ill|Mogasaki Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]], and the {{ill|Sōzenji Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:宗禅寺横穴墓群]] are found along the Hirose River, all collectively referred to as the {{ill|Mukaigaoka Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:向山横穴墓群]]. These tombs are believed to have been constructed from the late 7th century to the early 8th century. Approximately 2 kilometers southeast of this site is the {{ill|Kōriyama Ruins|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:郡山遺跡]], where the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:陸奥国]] was located at the time. It is speculated that these tombs were built by the people who lived in the capital and surrounding settlements.
{{right| [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9b.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Left-side cave]] [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9c.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Right-side cave (Photos taken in September 2006)]] ]]
In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a total of 34 tombs were found on the northern side of {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山]] and on both the north and south slopes of Mount Atago. Additionally, it is reported that over ten more tombs were destroyed within the next few years. A map from the time shows three tombs on the northern slope of Atagoyama, three on the eastern slope, 20 on the southeastern slope, and nine other unidentified or destroyed tombs. The exact locations of the tombs recorded in this survey are now unknown, as many were lost due to residential development and road construction, making it impossible to determine their precise number and placement.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴). The accompanying map was hand-drawn and does not accurately reflect the modern altered landscape. The text states that 34 tombs exist, but only 33 are depicted with slanted lines, while other types of tombs or destroyed tombs are shown without explanation.</ref>
Since [[1973]] (Shōwa 48), surveys have focused on the tombs on the southern slope, where 28 tombs have been confirmed. In addition, a single horizontal tomb with red murals was found near the southeastern slope. No excavations have been conducted on the northern side.
These tombs were built into the middle of the slopes, with a passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:羨道]]) approximately 1 meter wide leading to a slightly narrower entrance ({{ill|genmon|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄門]]), which then opens into the burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄室]]). Some tombs lack an entrance door. The length of the passage is unknown. The burial chambers are either rectangular or trapezoidal, sometimes with rounded corners, and most range from 1 to 3 meters per side. One tomb was found with stones laid over half of its floor.
Due to poor preservation conditions, the full range of burial goods is unclear. However, artifacts such as iron swords, iron arrowheads, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]], {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]], and {{ill|glass beads|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:ガラス玉]] have been found.
== Atagoyama Decorated Yokonahaka Burial Mound ==
Near the open tombs, a decorated horizontal tomb was discovered underground. The entrance passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:羨道]]) was 2.5 meters long and 1.15 meters wide at the bottom. The burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄室]]) was nearly square, measuring 1.8 meters (front), 1.9 meters (back), 1.8 meters (right), and 1.65 meters (left). The chamber is estimated to be about 1.4 meters high and shaped like either a house or a dome. The entrance appears to have been sealed with stacked stones, possibly with a door that has since disappeared. The construction of this tomb follows the same pattern as the others in the group.
The back wall of the burial chamber features decorations painted in red pigment, consisting of multiple circular and cross-shaped motifs arranged in a scattered pattern. Grave goods found in this tomb included one {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]] vessel, one small knife, the remains of five individuals, as well as unidentified iron objects, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]], and {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]] fragments.
This decorated tomb is estimated to date to the mid-to-late 7th century. The presence of murals suggests that a high-ranking individual may have been buried here. == Excavation History ==
The open cave tombs of {{ill|Mount Atago (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:愛宕山 (仙台市)]] have been known locally for a long time. A map published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1) records those on the northern side as {{ill|Emishi caves|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:蝦夷穴]].<ref>『最新版仙台全図』（『100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩』60頁）。</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), during road construction that cut into the mountain, numerous horizontal tombs were discovered, along with human remains, straight swords, and {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]]. However, all of these finds were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), p. 73.</ref>
The first systematic investigation of Atagoyama’s cave tombs was conducted by {{ill|Shimizu Toshiro|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:清水東四郎]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), when he reported a total of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), pp. 27–28.</ref> Later, {{ill|Ito Nobuo|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:伊東信雄]] also took measurements of one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), pp. 72–73. The exact date of this survey is not mentioned in the text and may have been postwar.</ref>
During World War II, the open tombs were repurposed as air-raid shelters, and after the war, some were used as household storage spaces. As Sendai expanded, urban development destroyed additional tombs.
When {{ill|Atago Bridge (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:愛宕大橋]] was constructed, its connecting roads cut into the mountain's edge, prompting an official excavation by the Sendai City authorities. In [[1973]], ten cave tombs were confirmed on the southern slope, and nine of them were excavated. During this survey, a single {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]] vessel and human bones were discovered.<ref>『仙台市向山愛宕山横穴群発掘調査報告書』。</ref>
On April 21, [[1976]] (Shōwa 51), roadwork near the southeastern slope suddenly revealed a tomb containing human bones. The {{ill|Sendai South Police Station|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:仙台南警察署]] was notified and determined that the remains were ancient, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. This tomb turned out to be the decorated horizontal burial mound, the most significant discovery among the Atagoyama tombs. Although the chamber’s wall paintings were recognized as an important find, there were no resources for preservation at the time, and the tomb was reburied after documentation.<ref>『宮城県仙台市愛宕山装飾横穴古墳発掘調査報告書』。</ref> The site is located just outside the curve of {{ill|Hirosegawa Riverside Road|en}}[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:広瀬河畔通り]].
In September and October of [[1991]] (Heisei 3), an excavation was conducted before the construction of new housing. This revealed 18 underground cave tombs, of which 15 were investigated. Many of these had been partially damaged before the excavation, but artifacts such as straight swords and glass beads were still recovered.<ref>『仙台市愛宕山横穴墓群 第3次発掘調査報告書』。</ref>

== Excavation History == The existence of open tombs in Atagoyama was well known locally, and they were marked as "[[Emishi Caves]]" (蝦夷穴) on maps published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1).<ref>"Latest Sendai City Map" (最新版仙台全図) in *100 Years Ago in Sendai: Sendai Map Walk* (100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩), p. 60.</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), road construction led to the discovery of numerous horizontal tombs, along with human remains, straight swords, and Sue ware. However, these artifacts were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," p. 73.</ref>
The first formal survey of Atagoyama's tombs was conducted by [[Shimizu Toshiro]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), who reported the existence of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," pp. 27-28.</ref> Later, [[Ito Nobuo]] also measured one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," pp. 72-73.</ref>
During [[World War II]], some of the open tombs were used as air-raid shelters and later repurposed as storage spaces for private homes. As Sendai expanded post-war, residential developments destroyed several tombs.
During the construction of [[Atago Bridge]], road construction along the mountainside led to an investigation by Sendai City. In [[1973]], ten tombs on the southern slope were identified, with nine of them excavated. This excavation yielded a single Sue ware vessel and human remains.<ref>*Sendai City Mukaigaoka Atagoyama Yokonahaka Group Excavation Report*</ref>
In [[1991]], a pre-construction excavation for residential development uncovered 18 underground tombs, of which 15 were surveyed. Many had been partially destroyed, but some yielded straight swords and glass beads.<ref>*Sendai City Atagoyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group: Third Excavation Report*</ref>

Daidenji]][[Category:qq]]

on {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山]], which are known as the {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山横穴墓群]]. Additionally, the {{ill|Futatsusawa Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:二ツ沢横穴墓群]], the {{ill|Mogasaki Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]], and the {{ill|Sōzenji Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:宗禅寺横穴墓群]] are found along the Hirose River, all collectively referred to as the {{ill|Mukaigaoka Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:向山横穴墓群]]. These tombs are believed to have been constructed from the late 7th century to the early 8th century. Approximately 2 kilometers southeast of this site is the {{ill|Kōriyama Ruins|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:郡山遺跡]], where the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:陸奥国]] was located at the time. It is speculated that these tombs were built by the people who lived in the capital and surrounding settlements.
{{right| [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9b.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Left-side cave]] [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9c.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Right-side cave (Photos taken in September 2006)]] ]]
In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a total of 34 tombs were found on the northern side of {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山]] and on both the north and south slopes of Mount Atago. Additionally, it is reported that over ten more tombs were destroyed within the next few years. A map from the time shows three tombs on the northern slope of Atagoyama, three on the eastern slope, 20 on the southeastern slope, and nine other unidentified or destroyed tombs. The exact locations of the tombs recorded in this survey are now unknown, as many were lost due to residential development and road construction, making it impossible to determine their precise number and placement.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴). The accompanying map was hand-drawn and does not accurately reflect the modern altered landscape. The text states that 34 tombs exist, but only 33 are depicted with slanted lines, while other types of tombs or destroyed tombs are shown without explanation.</ref>
Since [[1973]] (Shōwa 48), surveys have focused on the tombs on the southern slope, where 28 tombs have been confirmed. In addition, a single horizontal tomb with red murals was found near the southeastern slope. No excavations have been conducted on the northern side.
These tombs were built into the middle of the slopes, with a passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:羨道]]) approximately 1 meter wide leading to a slightly narrower entrance ({{ill|genmon|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄門]]), which then opens into the burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄室]]). Some tombs lack an entrance door. The length of the passage is unknown. The burial chambers are either rectangular or trapezoidal, sometimes with rounded corners, and most range from 1 to 3 meters per side. One tomb was found with stones laid over half of its floor.
Due to poor preservation conditions, the full range of burial goods is unclear. However, artifacts such as iron swords, iron arrowheads, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]], {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]], and {{ill|glass beads|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:ガラス玉]] have been found.
== Atagoyama Decorated Yokonahaka Burial Mound ==
Near the open tombs, a decorated horizontal tomb was discovered underground. The entrance passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:羨道]]) was 2.5 meters long and 1.15 meters wide at the bottom. The burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄室]]) was nearly square, measuring 1.8 meters (front), 1.9 meters (back), 1.8 meters (right), and 1.65 meters (left). The chamber is estimated to be about 1.4 meters high and shaped like either a house or a dome. The entrance appears to have been sealed with stacked stones, possibly with a door that has since disappeared. The construction of this tomb follows the same pattern as the others in the group.
The back wall of the burial chamber features decorations painted in red pigment, consisting of multiple circular and cross-shaped motifs arranged in a scattered pattern. Grave goods found in this tomb included one {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]] vessel, one small knife, the remains of five individuals, as well as unidentified iron objects, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]], and {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]] fragments.
This decorated tomb is estimated to date to the mid-to-late 7th century. The presence of murals suggests that a high-ranking individual may have been buried here. == Excavation History ==
The open cave tombs of {{ill|Mount Atago (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:愛宕山 (仙台市)]] have been known locally for a long time. A map published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1) records those on the northern side as {{ill|Emishi caves|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:蝦夷穴]].<ref>『最新版仙台全図』（『100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩』60頁）。</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), during road construction that cut into the mountain, numerous horizontal tombs were discovered, along with human remains, straight swords, and {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]]. However, all of these finds were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), p. 73.</ref>
The first systematic investigation of Atagoyama’s cave tombs was conducted by {{ill|Shimizu Toshiro|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:清水東四郎]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), when he reported a total of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), pp. 27–28.</ref> Later, {{ill|Ito Nobuo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:伊東信雄]] also took measurements of one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), pp. 72–73. The exact date of this survey is not mentioned in the text and may have been postwar.</ref>
During World War II, the open tombs were repurposed as air-raid shelters, and after the war, some were used as household storage spaces. As Sendai expanded, urban development destroyed additional tombs.
When {{ill|Atago Bridge (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:愛宕大橋]] was constructed, its connecting roads cut into the mountain's edge, prompting an official excavation by the Sendai City authorities. In [[1973]], ten cave tombs were confirmed on the southern slope, and nine of them were excavated. During this survey, a single {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]] vessel and human bones were discovered.<ref>『仙台市向山愛宕山横穴群発掘調査報告書』。</ref>
On April 21, [[1976]] (Shōwa 51), roadwork near the southeastern slope suddenly revealed a tomb containing human bones. The {{ill|Sendai South Police Station|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:仙台南警察署]] was notified and determined that the remains were ancient, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. This tomb turned out to be the decorated horizontal burial mound, the most significant discovery among the Atagoyama tombs. Although the chamber’s wall paintings were recognized as an important find, there were no resources for preservation at the time, and the tomb was reburied after documentation.<ref>『宮城県仙台市愛宕山装飾横穴古墳発掘調査報告書』。</ref> The site is located just outside the curve of {{ill|Hirosegawa Riverside Road|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:広瀬河畔通り]].
In September and October of [[1991]] (Heisei 3), an excavation was conducted before the construction of new housing. This revealed 18 underground cave tombs, of which 15 were investigated. Many of these had been partially damaged before the excavation, but artifacts such as straight swords and glass beads were still recovered.<ref>『仙台市愛宕山横穴墓群 第3次発掘調査報告書』。</ref>

== Excavation History == The existence of open tombs in Atagoyama was well known locally, and they were marked as "[[Emishi Caves]]" (蝦夷穴) on maps published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1).<ref>"Latest Sendai City Map" (最新版仙台全図) in *100 Years Ago in Sendai: Sendai Map Walk* (100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩), p. 60.</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), road construction led to the discovery of numerous horizontal tombs, along with human remains, straight swords, and Sue ware. However, these artifacts were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," p. 73.</ref>
The first formal survey of Atagoyama's tombs was conducted by [[Shimizu Toshiro]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), who reported the existence of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," pp. 27-28.</ref> Later, [[Ito Nobuo]] also measured one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," pp. 72-73.</ref>
During [[World War II]], some of the open tombs were used as air-raid shelters and later repurposed as storage spaces for private homes. As Sendai expanded post-war, residential developments destroyed several tombs.
During the construction of [[Atago Bridge]], road construction along the mountainside led to an investigation by Sendai City. In [[1973]], ten tombs on the southern slope were identified, with nine of them excavated. This excavation yielded a single Sue ware vessel and human remains.<ref>*Sendai City Mukaigaoka Atagoyama Yokonahaka Group Excavation Report*</ref>
In [[1991]], a pre-construction excavation for residential development uncovered 18 underground tombs, of which 15 were surveyed. Many had been partially destroyed, but some yielded straight swords and glass beads.<ref>*Sendai City Atagoyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group: Third Excavation Report*</ref>

on {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山]], which are known as the {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山横穴墓群]]. Additionally, the {{ill|Futatsusawa Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:二ツ沢横穴墓群]], the {{ill|Mogasaki Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]], and the {{ill|Sōzenji Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:宗禅寺横穴墓群]] are found along the Hirose River, all collectively referred to as the {{ill|Mukaigaoka Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:向山横穴墓群]]. These tombs are believed to have been constructed from the late 7th century to the early 8th century. Approximately 2 kilometers southeast of this site is the {{ill|Kōriyama Ruins|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:郡山遺跡]], where the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:陸奥国]] was located at the time. It is speculated that these tombs were built by the people who lived in the capital and surrounding settlements.
{{right| [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9b.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Left-side cave]] [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9c.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Right-side cave (Photos taken in September 2006)]] ]]
In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a total of 34 tombs were found on the northern side of {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大年寺山]] and on both the north and south slopes of Mount Atago. Additionally, it is reported that over ten more tombs were destroyed within the next few years. A map from the time shows three tombs on the northern slope of Atagoyama, three on the eastern slope, 20 on the southeastern slope, and nine other unidentified or destroyed tombs. The exact locations of the tombs recorded in this survey are now unknown, as many were lost due to residential development and road construction, making it impossible to determine their precise number and placement.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴). The accompanying map was hand-drawn and does not accurately reflect the modern altered landscape. The text states that 34 tombs exist, but only 33 are depicted with slanted lines, while other types of tombs or destroyed tombs are shown without explanation.</ref>
Since [[1973]] (Shōwa 48), surveys have focused on the tombs on the southern slope, where 28 tombs have been confirmed. In addition, a single horizontal tomb with red murals was found near the southeastern slope. No excavations have been conducted on the northern side.
These tombs were built into the middle of the slopes, with a passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:羨道]]) approximately 1 meter wide leading to a slightly narrower entrance ({{ill|genmon|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄門]]), which then opens into the burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄室]]). Some tombs lack an entrance door. The length of the passage is unknown. The burial chambers are either rectangular or trapezoidal, sometimes with rounded corners, and most range from 1 to 3 meters per side. One tomb was found with stones laid over half of its floor.
Due to poor preservation conditions, the full range of burial goods is unclear. However, artifacts such as iron swords, iron arrowheads, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]], {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]], and {{ill|glass beads|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:ガラス玉]] have been found.
== Atagoyama Decorated Yokonahaka Burial Mound ==
Near the open tombs, a decorated horizontal tomb was discovered underground. The entrance passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:羨道]]) was 2.5 meters long and 1.15 meters wide at the bottom. The burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:玄室]]) was nearly square, measuring 1.8 meters (front), 1.9 meters (back), 1.8 meters (right), and 1.65 meters (left). The chamber is estimated to be about 1.4 meters high and shaped like either a house or a dome. The entrance appears to have been sealed with stacked stones, possibly with a door that has since disappeared. The construction of this tomb follows the same pattern as the others in the group.
The back wall of the burial chamber features decorations painted in red pigment, consisting of multiple circular and cross-shaped motifs arranged in a scattered pattern. Grave goods found in this tomb included one {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]] vessel, one small knife, the remains of five individuals, as well as unidentified iron objects, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]], and {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:土師器]] fragments.
This decorated tomb is estimated to date to the mid-to-late 7th century. The presence of murals suggests that a high-ranking individual may have been buried here. == Excavation History ==
The open cave tombs of {{ill|Mount Atago (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:愛宕山 (仙台市)]] have been known locally for a long time. A map published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1) records those on the northern side as {{ill|Emishi caves|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:蝦夷穴]].<ref>『最新版仙台全図』（『100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩』60頁）。</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), during road construction that cut into the mountain, numerous horizontal tombs were discovered, along with human remains, straight swords, and {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]]. However, all of these finds were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), p. 73.</ref>
The first systematic investigation of Atagoyama’s cave tombs was conducted by {{ill|Shimizu Toshiro|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:清水東四郎]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), when he reported a total of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), pp. 27–28.</ref> Later, {{ill|Ito Nobuo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:伊東信雄]] also took measurements of one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), pp. 72–73. The exact date of this survey is not mentioned in the text and may have been postwar.</ref>
During World War II, the open tombs were repurposed as air-raid shelters, and after the war, some were used as household storage spaces. As Sendai expanded, urban development destroyed additional tombs.
When {{ill|Atago Bridge (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:愛宕大橋]] was constructed, its connecting roads cut into the mountain's edge, prompting an official excavation by the Sendai City authorities. In [[1973]], ten cave tombs were confirmed on the southern slope, and nine of them were excavated. During this survey, a single {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:須恵器]] vessel and human bones were discovered.<ref>『仙台市向山愛宕山横穴群発掘調査報告書』。</ref>
On April 21, [[1976]] (Shōwa 51), roadwork near the southeastern slope suddenly revealed a tomb containing human bones. The {{ill|Sendai South Police Station|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:仙台南警察署]] was notified and determined that the remains were ancient, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. This tomb turned out to be the decorated horizontal burial mound, the most significant discovery among the Atagoyama tombs. Although the chamber’s wall paintings were recognized as an important find, there were no resources for preservation at the time, and the tomb was reburied after documentation.<ref>『宮城県仙台市愛宕山装飾横穴古墳発掘調査報告書』。</ref> The site is located just outside the curve of {{ill|Hirosegawa Riverside Road|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:広瀬河畔通り]].
In September and October of [[1991]] (Heisei 3), an excavation was conducted before the construction of new housing. This revealed 18 underground cave tombs, of which 15 were investigated. Many of these had been partially damaged before the excavation, but artifacts such as straight swords and glass beads were still recovered.<ref>『仙台市愛宕山横穴墓群 第3次発掘調査報告書』。</ref>

== Excavation History == The existence of open tombs in Atagoyama was well known locally, and they were marked as "[[Emishi Caves]]" (蝦夷穴) on maps published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1).<ref>"Latest Sendai City Map" (最新版仙台全図) in *100 Years Ago in Sendai: Sendai Map Walk* (100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩), p. 60.</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), road construction led to the discovery of numerous horizontal tombs, along with human remains, straight swords, and Sue ware. However, these artifacts were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," p. 73.</ref>
The first formal survey of Atagoyama's tombs was conducted by [[Shimizu Toshiro]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), who reported the existence of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," pp. 27-28.</ref> Later, [[Ito Nobuo]] also measured one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," pp. 72-73.</ref>
During [[World War II]], some of the open tombs were used as air-raid shelters and later repurposed as storage spaces for private homes. As Sendai expanded post-war, residential developments destroyed several tombs.
During the construction of [[Atago Bridge]], road construction along the mountainside led to an investigation by Sendai City. In [[1973]], ten tombs on the southern slope were identified, with nine of them excavated. This excavation yielded a single Sue ware vessel and human remains.<ref>*Sendai City Mukaigaoka Atagoyama Yokonahaka Group Excavation Report*</ref>
In [[1991]], a pre-construction excavation for residential development uncovered 18 underground tombs, of which 15 were surveyed. Many had been partially destroyed, but some yielded straight swords and glass beads.<ref>*Sendai City Atagoyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group: Third Excavation Report*</ref>
