on {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}} [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:大年寺山]], which are known as the {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:大年寺山横穴墓群]]. Additionally, the {{ill|Futatsusawa Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:二ツ沢横穴墓群]], the {{ill|Mogasaki Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]], and the {{ill|Sōzenji Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:宗禅寺横穴墓群]] are found along the Hirose River, all collectively referred to as the {{ill|Mukaigaoka Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:向山横穴墓群]]. These tombs are believed to have been constructed from the late 7th century to the early 8th century. Approximately 2 kilometers southeast of this site is the {{ill|Kōriyama Ruins|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:郡山遺跡]], where the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:陸奥国]] was located at the time. It is speculated that these tombs were built by the people who lived in the capital and surrounding settlements.
{{right| [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9b.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Left-side cave]] [[image:AtagoyamaYokoanaBogun2006-9c.jpg|thumb|240px|none|Right-side cave (Photos taken in September 2006)]] ]]
In [[1938]] (Shōwa 13), a total of 34 tombs were found on the northern side of {{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:大年寺山]] and on both the north and south slopes of Mount Atago. Additionally, it is reported that over ten more tombs were destroyed within the next few years. A map from the time shows three tombs on the northern slope of Atagoyama, three on the eastern slope, 20 on the southeastern slope, and nine other unidentified or destroyed tombs. The exact locations of the tombs recorded in this survey are now unknown, as many were lost due to residential development and road construction, making it impossible to determine their precise number and placement.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴). The accompanying map was hand-drawn and does not accurately reflect the modern altered landscape. The text states that 34 tombs exist, but only 33 are depicted with slanted lines, while other types of tombs or destroyed tombs are shown without explanation.</ref>
Since [[1973]] (Shōwa 48), surveys have focused on the tombs on the southern slope, where 28 tombs have been confirmed. In addition, a single horizontal tomb with red murals was found near the southeastern slope. No excavations have been conducted on the northern side.
These tombs were built into the middle of the slopes, with a passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:羨道]]) approximately 1 meter wide leading to a slightly narrower entrance ({{ill|genmon|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:玄門]]), which then opens into the burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:玄室]]). Some tombs lack an entrance door. The length of the passage is unknown. The burial chambers are either rectangular or trapezoidal, sometimes with rounded corners, and most range from 1 to 3 meters per side. One tomb was found with stones laid over half of its floor.
Due to poor preservation conditions, the full range of burial goods is unclear. However, artifacts such as iron swords, iron arrowheads, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:須恵器]], {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:土師器]], and {{ill|glass beads|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:ガラス玉]] have been found.
== Atagoyama Decorated Yokonahaka Burial Mound ==
Near the open tombs, a decorated horizontal tomb was discovered underground. The entrance passage ({{ill|yūdo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:羨道]]) was 2.5 meters long and 1.15 meters wide at the bottom. The burial chamber ({{ill|genshitsu|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:玄室]]) was nearly square, measuring 1.8 meters (front), 1.9 meters (back), 1.8 meters (right), and 1.65 meters (left). The chamber is estimated to be about 1.4 meters high and shaped like either a house or a dome. The entrance appears to have been sealed with stacked stones, possibly with a door that has since disappeared. The construction of this tomb follows the same pattern as the others in the group.
The back wall of the burial chamber features decorations painted in red pigment, consisting of multiple circular and cross-shaped motifs arranged in a scattered pattern. Grave goods found in this tomb included one {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:土師器]] vessel, one small knife, the remains of five individuals, as well as unidentified iron objects, {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:須恵器]], and {{ill|Haji ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:土師器]] fragments.
This decorated tomb is estimated to date to the mid-to-late 7th century. The presence of murals suggests that a high-ranking individual may have been buried here. == Excavation History ==
The open cave tombs of {{ill|Mount Atago (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:愛宕山 (仙台市)]] have been known locally for a long time. A map published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1) records those on the northern side as {{ill|Emishi caves|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:蝦夷穴]].<ref>『最新版仙台全図』（『100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩』60頁）。</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), during road construction that cut into the mountain, numerous horizontal tombs were discovered, along with human remains, straight swords, and {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:須恵器]]. However, all of these finds were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), p. 73.</ref>
The first systematic investigation of Atagoyama’s cave tombs was conducted by {{ill|Shimizu Toshiro|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:清水東四郎]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), when he reported a total of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture" (宮城県の古碑及横穴), pp. 27–28.</ref> Later, {{ill|Ito Nobuo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:伊東信雄]] also took measurements of one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins of Sendai City" (仙台市内の古代遺跡), pp. 72–73. The exact date of this survey is not mentioned in the text and may have been postwar.</ref>
During World War II, the open tombs were repurposed as air-raid shelters, and after the war, some were used as household storage spaces. As Sendai expanded, urban development destroyed additional tombs.
When {{ill|Atago Bridge (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:愛宕大橋]] was constructed, its connecting roads cut into the mountain's edge, prompting an official excavation by the Sendai City authorities. In [[1973]], ten cave tombs were confirmed on the southern slope, and nine of them were excavated. During this survey, a single {{ill|Sue ware|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:須恵器]] vessel and human bones were discovered.<ref>『仙台市向山愛宕山横穴群発掘調査報告書』。</ref>
On April 21, [[1976]] (Shōwa 51), roadwork near the southeastern slope suddenly revealed a tomb containing human bones. The {{ill|Sendai South Police Station|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:仙台南警察署]] was notified and determined that the remains were ancient, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. This tomb turned out to be the decorated horizontal burial mound, the most significant discovery among the Atagoyama tombs. Although the chamber’s wall paintings were recognized as an important find, there were no resources for preservation at the time, and the tomb was reburied after documentation.<ref>『宮城県仙台市愛宕山装飾横穴古墳発掘調査報告書』。</ref> The site is located just outside the curve of {{ill|Hirosegawa Riverside Road|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Mount Daidenji-qq]] [[ja:広瀬河畔通り]].
In September and October of [[1991]] (Heisei 3), an excavation was conducted before the construction of new housing. This revealed 18 underground cave tombs, of which 15 were investigated. Many of these had been partially damaged before the excavation, but artifacts such as straight swords and glass beads were still recovered.<ref>『仙台市愛宕山横穴墓群 第3次発掘調査報告書』。</ref>

== Excavation History == The existence of open tombs in Atagoyama was well known locally, and they were marked as "[[Emishi Caves]]" (蝦夷穴) on maps published in [[1912]] (Taishō 1).<ref>"Latest Sendai City Map" (最新版仙台全図) in *100 Years Ago in Sendai: Sendai Map Walk* (100年前の仙台を歩く 仙台地図散歩), p. 60.</ref>
In [[1936]] (Shōwa 11), road construction led to the discovery of numerous horizontal tombs, along with human remains, straight swords, and Sue ware. However, these artifacts were lost.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," p. 28. Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," p. 73.</ref>
The first formal survey of Atagoyama's tombs was conducted by [[Shimizu Toshiro]] in [[1937]] (Shōwa 12), who reported the existence of 34 tombs on the southeastern and northern slopes.<ref>Shimizu Toshiro, "Ancient Monuments and Horizontal Tombs of Miyagi Prefecture," pp. 27-28.</ref> Later, [[Ito Nobuo]] also measured one of the tombs.<ref>Ito Nobuo, "Ancient Ruins in Sendai City," pp. 72-73.</ref>
During [[World War II]], some of the open tombs were used as air-raid shelters and later repurposed as storage spaces for private homes. As Sendai expanded post-war, residential developments destroyed several tombs.
During the construction of [[Atago Bridge]], road construction along the mountainside led to an investigation by Sendai City. In [[1973]], ten tombs on the southern slope were identified, with nine of them excavated. This excavation yielded a single Sue ware vessel and human remains.<ref>*Sendai City Mukaigaoka Atagoyama Yokonahaka Group Excavation Report*</ref>
In [[1991]], a pre-construction excavation for residential development uncovered 18 underground tombs, of which 15 were surveyed. Many had been partially destroyed, but some yielded straight swords and glass beads.<ref>*Sendai City Atagoyama Yokonahaka Burial Mound Group: Third Excavation Report*</ref>

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''大年寺山'''（だいねんじやま）は、[[宮城県]][[仙台市]][[太白区]]にある[[山]]である。山の名は[[江戸時代]]からこの山にある[[黄檗宗]][[大年寺|両足山大年寺]]に由来する。古くは'''野出口山'''、また'''茂ヶ崎'''と呼ばれた。大年寺公園とその一部である[[仙台市野草園]]があり、他に放送局のテレビ塔3本が建つ。[[標高]]は約120[[メートル]]。 {{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|大年寺惣門（2007年11月）]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|伊達家の墓所（2007年11月）]] == 地理 == 大年寺山は、[[仙台市都心部]]から見て南側、[[広瀬川 (宮城県)|広瀬川]]や[[愛宕山 (仙台市)|愛宕山]]、大窪谷地を隔てた所にある。大年寺山の南側には[[長町 (仙台市)|長町]]地区が広がる。 山の形は東北東から西南西に長い。この山の最高点とされてきた二等[[三角点]]「大年寺」（{{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=旧・二等三角点「大年寺」}}）は[[標高]]119.55メートルだったが、現在は停止（移転）している。 南西斜面に[[東北工業大学]]長町キャンパス（{{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=東北工業大学・長町キャンパス}}）がある。北西側斜面に仙台市野草園（{{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=仙台市野草園}}）があり、山の東側は[[大年寺公園]]で、[[伊達氏]]代々の墓所（{{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=伊達家の墓所}}）がある。北東側の山裾は広瀬川に近い。 == 歴史 == [[古墳時代]]にはこの山の中腹にたくさんの[[横穴墓]]が作られた。山の北側に[[大年寺山横穴墓群]]、南側に[[二ツ沢横穴墓群]]と[[茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]]、そのほか[[愛宕山横穴墓群]]や[[宗禅寺横穴墓群]]などがあり、全体で「[[向山横穴墓群]]」と称す[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html 茂ケ崎横穴墓群]（[[仙台市教育委員会]]）。 [[中世]]には茂ヶ崎と呼ばれ、[[茂ヶ崎城]]が置かれた。 [[1696年]]（[[元禄]]9年）、[[伊達綱村]]は[[廃寺]]になっていた仙英寺を茂ヶ崎に移し、大規模な寺院の造営に乗り出した。翌年、[[黄檗宗]]の鉄牛[[和尚]]が招かれ両足山大年寺を開いた。これ以後、[[江戸]]で死去した者を除く伊達家代々の墓所となり、江戸時代にはその保護を受けて広壮な伽藍を営んだ。当時の大年寺は、全国の黄檗宗の寺院の中でも規模が大きいものであった。[[明治]]になってから[[廃仏毀釈]]の風潮を受けて伊達家が仏式を止めたため、荒廃した。今も残る建築物は南の入り口にある惣門（{{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=（旧）大年寺惣門}}）だけである。 [[1918年]]（[[大正]]7年）には、[[労働者]]60余人が大年寺山に[[籠城|立てこもった]]。これは[[名取郡]]長町村の東北板紙での[[労働争議]]によるものであり、労働者は賃上げを要求して勝ち取った。日本と宮城県の労働運動黎明期の一事件である。 伊達家との関係が切れた黄檗宗は、[[昭和]]の初めに大年寺を再興した。これが現在の大年寺で、昔の門前にあたる山麓にある（{{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=（現）大年寺}}）。 [[1934年]]（昭和9年）11月に北隣の[[八木山 (宮城県)|八木山]]とあわせて308.32[[ヘクタール]]が「八木山大年寺[[風致地区]]」に指定され、仙台近郊の緑地として開発を抑制された1955年刊『仙台市史』第2巻361頁。。 伊達家の墓所があることから大年寺山では長い間、樹林の伐採は行われていなかった。しかし、第二次大戦中から戦後にかけて木材の需要が急増した影響で、大年寺山の樹林の伐採が行われた。[[1950年]]（昭和25年）に伊達家がここの山林を売却したために樹林の伐採が進み、大年寺山の景観は一変するほどだった『仙台市史』特別編9（地域史）484頁。。 [[1950年]]（昭和25年）に植物園の計画が持ち上がり、[[1954年]]（昭和29年）7月21日に[[仙台市野草園]]が開園した。この敷地は[[1945年]]（昭和20年）に地すべりを起こしていた所であり、野草園の設置はその有効活用という側面を持ち合わせていた。[[1956年]]（昭和31年）3月21日、NHK仙台総合テレビジョンの開局を先駆けに、山頂には各社のテレビ放送の塔が立ち並んだ。 仙台市は[[石井亨]]市長のもとで伊達家の墓所も含め大年寺山に公園を整備する構想を立て、土地取得を進めた。この過程で仙台市が[[1991年]]（[[平成]]3年）と[[1992年]]（平成4年）に4倍の費用で土地を購入したことが[[1993年]]（平成5年）[[9月]]に明るみに出た。[[市民団体]]の[[仙台市民オンブズマン]]は、土地を売却した4社を相手取って代金返還[[代位]]請求[[訴訟]]を[[11月]]に起こした。[[最高裁判所 (日本)|最高裁]]まで争われたこの[[裁判]]では、[[予算]]・[[決算]]報告を起点にして計算した請求期間1年をすぎてからの[[住民監査請求]]は認められないとの[[判決]]が[[2003年]]（平成15年）に確定した。 == テレビ塔 == {{座標一覧|section=テレビ塔}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|テレビ塔が立ち並ぶ大年寺山]] 外観上の特徴は、山上に立つ3本のテレビ塔である。東から、 * [[宮城テレビ放送]]（MMT。{{ウィキ座標|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|地図|name=宮城テレビ放送のテレビ塔}}） : 通称：「[https://www.mmt-tv.co.jp/mmttower/ ミヤテレタワー]」 : 高さ：138メートル : 概観：白 : 夜間[[ライトアップ]]：翌日の[[天気予報]]が、晴れならオレンジ色、曇りなら白色、雨・雪は緑色の照明となる。 : 鉄塔の中層部には仙台市街地向けの[[情報カメラ]]が設置されている。 * {{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>
== Related Topics == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局}}

== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|ja|横穴墓}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Yokoana Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Yokoana Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashi Nihon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
