{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>
== See Also == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局}}

From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

<!--I think this will be the last forking operation I do as I am trying to get this unwieldy wiki a bit more in control before winding down the project-->
{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/> == See Also! == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局}}

In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

<!--I think this will be the last forking operation I do as I am trying to get this unwieldy wiki a bit more in control before winding down the project-->
{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/> == See Also == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局}}
{{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}} is a mountain with {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Kofun Group|en}}

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=draft}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=draft}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|12=draft}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=draft}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=draft}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=draft}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=draft}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=draft}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|12=draft}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=draft}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村|12=draft}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=draft}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗|12=draft}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=draft}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=draft}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|12=draft}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|12=draft}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=draft}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送|12=draft}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送|12=draft}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送|12=draft}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送|12=draft}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=draft}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>
== See Also == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局|12=draft}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局|12=draft}}
{{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}} is a mountain with {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Kofun Group|en|12=draft}}

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=draft}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=draft}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|12=draft}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=draft}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=draft}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=draft}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=draft}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=draft}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|12=draft}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=draft}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村|12=draft}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=draft}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗|12=draft}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=draft}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=draft}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|12=draft}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|12=draft}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=draft}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送|12=draft}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送|12=draft}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送|12=draft}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送|12=draft}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=draft}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=draft}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=draft}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|12=draft}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=draft}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=draft}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=draft}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=draft}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=draft}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|12=draft}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=draft}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村|12=draft}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=draft}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗|12=draft}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=draft}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=draft}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|12=draft}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|12=draft}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=draft}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送|12=draft}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送|12=draft}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送|12=draft}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送|12=draft}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=draft}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>
== See Also == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局|12=draft}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局|12=draft}}

Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=draft}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|12=draft}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=draft}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村|12=draft}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=draft}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗|12=draft}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=draft}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=draft}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|12=draft}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|12=draft}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=draft}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{座標一覧|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送|12=draft}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送|12=draft}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送|12=draft}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送|12=draft}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=draft}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=draft}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=draft}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|12=draft}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.

On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=draft|12=draft}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}}. {{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=draft|12=draft}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft|12=draft}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=draft|12=draft}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=draft|12=draft}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft|12=draft}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=draft|12=draft}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=draft|12=draft}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|12=draft|12=draft}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=draft|12=draft}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=draft|12=draft}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|12=draft|12=draft}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=draft|12=draft}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村|12=draft|12=draft}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=draft|12=draft}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗|12=draft|12=draft}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=draft|12=draft}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=draft|12=draft}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|12=draft|12=draft}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=draft|12=draft}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送|12=draft|12=draft}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送|12=draft|12=draft}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送|12=draft|12=draft}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送|12=draft|12=draft}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=draft|12=draft}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>
== See Also == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局|12=draft|12=draft}}
{{ill|Mount Daidenji|en}} is a mountain with {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Kofun Group|en|12=draft|12=draft}}
