{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|1=Meiji era}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''大年寺山'''（だいねんじやま）は、[[宮城県]][[仙台市]][[太白区]]にある[[山]]である。山の名は[[江戸時代]]からこの山にある[[黄檗宗]][[大年寺|両足山大年寺]]に由来する。古くは'''野出口山'''、また'''茂ヶ崎'''と呼ばれた。大年寺公園とその一部である[[仙台市野草園]]があり、他に放送局のテレビ塔3本が建つ。[[標高]]は約120[[メートル]]。 {{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|大年寺惣門（2007年11月）]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|伊達家の墓所（2007年11月）]] == 地理 == 大年寺山は、[[仙台市都心部]]から見て南側、[[広瀬川 (宮城県)|広瀬川]]や[[愛宕山 (仙台市)|愛宕山]]、大窪谷地を隔てた所にある。大年寺山の南側には[[長町 (仙台市)|長町]]地区が広がる。 山の形は東北東から西南西に長い。この山の最高点とされてきた二等[[三角点]]「大年寺」（{{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=旧・二等三角点「大年寺」}}）は[[標高]]119.55メートルだったが、現在は停止（移転）している。 南西斜面に[[東北工業大学]]長町キャンパス（{{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=東北工業大学・長町キャンパス}}）がある。北西側斜面に仙台市野草園（{{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=仙台市野草園}}）があり、山の東側は[[大年寺公園]]で、[[伊達氏]]代々の墓所（{{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=伊達家の墓所}}）がある。北東側の山裾は広瀬川に近い。 == 歴史 == [[古墳時代]]にはこの山の中腹にたくさんの[[横穴墓]]が作られた。山の北側に[[大年寺山横穴墓群]]、南側に[[二ツ沢横穴墓群]]と[[茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]]、そのほか[[愛宕山横穴墓群]]や[[宗禅寺横穴墓群]]などがあり、全体で「[[向山横穴墓群]]」と称す[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html 茂ケ崎横穴墓群]（[[仙台市教育委員会]]）。 [[中世]]には茂ヶ崎と呼ばれ、[[茂ヶ崎城]]が置かれた。 [[1696年]]（[[元禄]]9年）、[[伊達綱村]]は[[廃寺]]になっていた仙英寺を茂ヶ崎に移し、大規模な寺院の造営に乗り出した。翌年、[[黄檗宗]]の鉄牛[[和尚]]が招かれ両足山大年寺を開いた。これ以後、[[江戸]]で死去した者を除く伊達家代々の墓所となり、江戸時代にはその保護を受けて広壮な伽藍を営んだ。当時の大年寺は、全国の黄檗宗の寺院の中でも規模が大きいものであった。[[明治]]になってから[[廃仏毀釈]]の風潮を受けて伊達家が仏式を止めたため、荒廃した。今も残る建築物は南の入り口にある惣門（{{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=（旧）大年寺惣門}}）だけである。 [[1918年]]（[[大正]]7年）には、[[労働者]]60余人が大年寺山に[[籠城|立てこもった]]。これは[[名取郡]]長町村の東北板紙での[[労働争議]]によるものであり、労働者は賃上げを要求して勝ち取った。日本と宮城県の労働運動黎明期の一事件である。 伊達家との関係が切れた黄檗宗は、[[昭和]]の初めに大年寺を再興した。これが現在の大年寺で、昔の門前にあたる山麓にある（{{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=（現）大年寺}}）。 [[1934年]]（昭和9年）11月に北隣の[[八木山 (宮城県)|八木山]]とあわせて308.32[[ヘクタール]]が「八木山大年寺[[風致地区]]」に指定され、仙台近郊の緑地として開発を抑制された1955年刊『仙台市史』第2巻361頁。。 伊達家の墓所があることから大年寺山では長い間、樹林の伐採は行われていなかった。しかし、第二次大戦中から戦後にかけて木材の需要が急増した影響で、大年寺山の樹林の伐採が行われた。[[1950年]]（昭和25年）に伊達家がここの山林を売却したために樹林の伐採が進み、大年寺山の景観は一変するほどだった『仙台市史』特別編9（地域史）484頁。。 [[1950年]]（昭和25年）に植物園の計画が持ち上がり、[[1954年]]（昭和29年）7月21日に[[仙台市野草園]]が開園した。この敷地は[[1945年]]（昭和20年）に地すべりを起こしていた所であり、野草園の設置はその有効活用という側面を持ち合わせていた。[[1956年]]（昭和31年）3月21日、NHK仙台総合テレビジョンの開局を先駆けに、山頂には各社のテレビ放送の塔が立ち並んだ。 仙台市は[[石井亨]]市長のもとで伊達家の墓所も含め大年寺山に公園を整備する構想を立て、土地取得を進めた。この過程で仙台市が[[1991年]]（[[平成]]3年）と[[1992年]]（平成4年）に4倍の費用で土地を購入したことが[[1993年]]（平成5年）[[9月]]に明るみに出た。[[市民団体]]の[[仙台市民オンブズマン]]は、土地を売却した4社を相手取って代金返還[[代位]]請求[[訴訟]]を[[11月]]に起こした。[[最高裁判所 (日本)|最高裁]]まで争われたこの[[裁判]]では、[[予算]]・[[決算]]報告を起点にして計算した請求期間1年をすぎてからの[[住民監査請求]]は認められないとの[[判決]]が[[2003年]]（平成15年）に確定した。 == テレビ塔 == {{座標一覧|section=テレビ塔}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|テレビ塔が立ち並ぶ大年寺山]] 外観上の特徴は、山上に立つ3本のテレビ塔である。東から、 * [[宮城テレビ放送]]（MMT。{{ウィキ座標|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|地図|name=宮城テレビ放送のテレビ塔}}） : 通称：「[https://www.mmt-tv.co.jp/mmttower/ ミヤテレタワー]」 : 高さ：138メートル : 概観：白 : 夜間[[ライトアップ]]：翌日の[[天気予報]]が、晴れならオレンジ色、曇りなら白色、雨・雪は緑色の照明となる。 : 鉄塔の中層部には仙台市街地向けの[[情報カメラ]]が設置されている。 * [[NHK仙台放送局]]・[[東北放送]]（TBC）・[[東日本放送]]（KHB）の共同。（{{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK仙台放送局・東北放送（地デジ専用）・東日本放送の共同のテレビ塔}}） : 高さ：150メートル : 概観：白 : 夜間ライトアップ：なし : 2001年に地上デジタルテレビ放送の整備に合わせ、建て替え。同時にKHBのアナログ送信アンテナがMMTの鉄塔から移設された（MMTのデジタルテレビ放送用アンテナを設置するため）。 : 3局の地上デジタルテレビ放送とNHK-FMラジオ放送の送信施設として運用されている。2012年3月31日までは、NHKとKHBの地上アナログテレビ放送も運用されていた。 : こちらには、NHKの情報カメラが南側（[[長町南駅]]方向）を向けて設置されている。 * [[仙台放送]]（OX・[[エフエム仙台]]（Date fm）が共用。{{ウィキ座標|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|地図|name=仙台放送のテレビ塔（FMSが共用）}}） : 通称：「[[仙台スカイキャンドル]]」（2012年6月命名） : 高さ：147.7{{Cite web|和書|title=仙台放送／仙台スカイキャンドル |url=https://www.ox-tv.co.jp/company/sendai-sky-candle.html |website=www.ox-tv.co.jp |access-date=2022-06-04}}メートル : 概観：赤白 : 夜間ライトアップ：1時間単位で照明の色が変化する。 : [[2004年]]11月までは、塔下にあるスタジオから番組を送り出していた。 : [[2016年]]6月30日までは[[ジャパン・モバイルキャスティング|モバキャス]]（[[NOTTV]]）の送信設備が設置されていた。 上記の3つの鉄塔がある大年寺山の西隣の八木山にテレビ塔として運用されていた鉄塔がある。 * 東北放送（TBC。{{ウィキ座標|38|14|48.9|N|140|51|19.3|E|region:JP|地図|name=東北放送のテレビ塔（地上アナログテレビ専用）}}） : 通称 : 通称：トリシャイン : 高さ：120メートル : 概観：赤白 : 夜間ライトアップ：3色の照明で模様をつくる。 : 2012年3月31日まで、地上アナログテレビ放送の送信施設として運用されていた。 : 2017年5月より[[FM補完中継局|FMラジオ放送]]の送信施設として運用を開始。 八木山の東北放送を含めた4本中3本の「テレビ塔ライトアップ」は、第10回仙台市都市景観大賞を受賞した[http://www.city.sendai.jp/soumu/kouhou/press/08-01-15/keikan2.html 第10回仙台市都市景観大賞]（仙台市）。[[東京]]からの[[東北新幹線]]下りの車中から「テレビ塔ライトアップ」は非常に良く見え、仙台到着の[[ランドマーク]]となっていることが受賞理由となっている。 なお、[[仙台空港]]の[[航空法]]の[[制限表面]]のうち円錐表面と外部水平表面は仙台市中心部には設定されておらず、これらのテレビ塔は建設が可能であった（[[仙台の高層ビル一覧#制限表面|参照]]）[https://www.mlit.go.jp/tokyo_cab/06_oshirase/index_02_img/sendai.pdf 仙台空港の制限表面図]（[[国土交通省]]東京航空局）。 [[宮城県]]の地上デジタル放送における[[リモコンキーID]]は、全国で唯一、[[キー局|系列局]]の割り当てが[[鹿児島県]]と同一になっている。 また、本項では、2012年[[12月14日]]から2016年[[6月30日]]まで運用されていた[[ジャパン・モバイルキャスティング]]運営の[[NOTTV]]仙台送信所についても併せて記述する。 === 地上デジタルテレビジョン放送送信設備 revision.text:
{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''大年寺山'''（だいねんじやま）は、[[宮城県]][[仙台市]][[太白区]]にある[[山]]である。山の名は[[江戸時代]]からこの山にある[[黄檗宗]][[大年寺|両足山大年寺]]に由来する。古くは'''野出口山'''、また'''茂ヶ崎'''と呼ばれた。大年寺公園とその一部である[[仙台市野草園]]があり、他に放送局のテレビ塔3本が建つ。[[標高]]は約120[[メートル]]。 {{座標一覧}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|大年寺惣門（2007年11月）]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|伊達家の墓所（2007年11月）]] == 地理 == 大年寺山は、[[仙台市都心部]]から見て南側、[[広瀬川 (宮城県)|広瀬川]]や[[愛宕山 (仙台市)|愛宕山]]、大窪谷地を隔てた所にある。大年寺山の南側には[[長町 (仙台市)|長町]]地区が広がる。 山の形は東北東から西南西に長い。この山の最高点とされてきた二等[[三角点]]「大年寺」（{{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=旧・二等三角点「大年寺」}}）は[[標高]]119.55メートルだったが、現在は停止（移転）している。 南西斜面に[[東北工業大学]]長町キャンパス（{{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=東北工業大学・長町キャンパス}}）がある。北西側斜面に仙台市野草園（{{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=仙台市野草園}}）があり、山の東側は[[大年寺公園]]で、[[伊達氏]]代々の墓所（{{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=伊達家の墓所}}）がある。北東側の山裾は広瀬川に近い。 == 歴史 == [[古墳時代]]にはこの山の中腹にたくさんの[[横穴墓]]が作られた。山の北側に[[大年寺山横穴墓群]]、南側に[[二ツ沢横穴墓群]]と[[茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]]、そのほか[[愛宕山横穴墓群]]や[[宗禅寺横穴墓群]]などがあり、全体で「[[向山横穴墓群]]」と称す[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html 茂ケ崎横穴墓群]（[[仙台市教育委員会]]）。 [[中世]]には茂ヶ崎と呼ばれ、[[茂ヶ崎城]]が置かれた。 [[1696年]]（[[元禄]]9年）、[[伊達綱村]]は[[廃寺]]になっていた仙英寺を茂ヶ崎に移し、大規模な寺院の造営に乗り出した。翌年、[[黄檗宗]]の鉄牛[[和尚]]が招かれ両足山大年寺を開いた。これ以後、[[江戸]]で死去した者を除く伊達家代々の墓所となり、江戸時代にはその保護を受けて広壮な伽藍を営んだ。当時の大年寺は、全国の黄檗宗の寺院の中でも規模が大きいものであった。[[明治]]になってから[[廃仏毀釈]]の風潮を受けて伊達家が仏式を止めたため、荒廃した。今も残る建築物は南の入り口にある惣門（{{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=（旧）大年寺惣門}}）だけである。 [[1918年]]（[[大正]]7年）には、[[労働者]]60余人が大年寺山に[[籠城|立てこもった]]。これは[[名取郡]]長町村の東北板紙での[[労働争議]]によるものであり、労働者は賃上げを要求して勝ち取った。日本と宮城県の労働運動黎明期の一事件である。 伊達家との関係が切れた黄檗宗は、[[昭和]]の初めに大年寺を再興した。これが現在の大年寺で、昔の門前にあたる山麓にある（{{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=（現）大年寺}}）。 [[1934年]]（昭和9年）11月に北隣の[[八木山 (宮城県)|八木山]]とあわせて308.32[[ヘクタール]]が「八木山大年寺[[風致地区]]」に指定され、仙台近郊の緑地として開発を抑制された1955年刊『仙台市史』第2巻361頁。。 伊達家の墓所があることから大年寺山では長い間、樹林の伐採は行われていなかった。しかし、第二次大戦中から戦後にかけて木材の需要が急増した影響で、大年寺山の樹林の伐採が行われた。[[1950年]]（昭和25年）に伊達家がここの山林を売却したために樹林の伐採が進み、大年寺山の景観は一変するほどだった『仙台市史』特別編9（地域史）484頁。。 [[1950年]]（昭和25年）に植物園の計画が持ち上がり、[[1954年]]（昭和29年）7月21日に[[仙台市野草園]]が開園した。この敷地は[[1945年]]（昭和20年）に地すべりを起こしていた所であり、野草園の設置はその有効活用という側面を持ち合わせていた。[[1956年]]（昭和31年）3月21日、NHK仙台総合テレビジョンの開局を先駆けに、山頂には各社のテレビ放送の塔が立ち並んだ。 仙台市は[[石井亨]]市長のもとで伊達家の墓所も含め大年寺山に公園を整備する構想を立て、土地取得を進めた。この過程で仙台市が[[1991年]]（[[平成]]3年）と[[1992年]]（平成4年）に4倍の費用で土地を購入したことが[[1993年]]（平成5年）[[9月]]に明るみに出た。[[市民団体]]の[[仙台市民オンブズマン]]は、土地を売却した4社を相手取って代金返還[[代位]]請求[[訴訟]]を[[11月]]に起こした。[[最高裁判所 (日本)|最高裁]]まで争われたこの[[裁判]]では、[[予算]]・[[決算]]報告を起点にして計算した請求期間1年をすぎてからの[[住民監査請求]]は認められないとの[[判決]]が[[2003年]]（平成15年）に確定した。 == テレビ塔 == {{座標一覧|section=テレビ塔}} {{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城}}.

In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=draft}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=draft}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].

The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|12=draft}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.

However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|12=draft}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.

On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=draft}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=draft}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=draft}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=draft}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=draft}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|12=draft}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=draft}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村|12=draft}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=draft}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗|12=draft}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=draft}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=draft}}. Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|12=draft}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|12=draft}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=draft}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|qq=draft}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|qq=draft}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].

The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|qq=draft}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|qq=draft}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|qq=draft}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|qq=draft}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|qq=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|qq=draft}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|qq=draft}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|qq=draft}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|qq=draft}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|qq=draft}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|qq=draft}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|qq=draft}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|qq=draft}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村|qq=draft}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|qq=draft}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗|qq=draft}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|qq=draft}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|qq=draft}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|qq=draft}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|qq=draft}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|qq=draft}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送|qq=draft}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送|qq=draft}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送|qq=draft}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送|qq=draft}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|qq=draft}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>

From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji era|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji era|qq=}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haibutsu kishaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Haibutsu kishaku|qq=}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōwa era|qq=}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|qq=}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|qq=}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|qq=}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|qq=}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|qq=}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangulation point|qq=}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Middle Ages|qq=}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|qq=}}.

In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|qq=}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|qq=}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|qq=}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|qq=}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|qq=}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation point|ja|三角点|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangulation point|qq=}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Middle Ages|qq=}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|qq=}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Tsunamura|qq=}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|qq=}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōbaku sect|qq=}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|qq=}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|qq=}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji era|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji era|qq=}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haibutsu kishaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Haibutsu kishaku|qq=}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōwa era|qq=}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|qq=}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyagi Television Broadcasting|qq=}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/NHK Sendai|qq=}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Broadcasting|qq=}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashinippon Broadcasting|qq=}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Broadcasting|qq=}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|qq=}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>
== See Also == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Television Relay Stations|qq=}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/New World Nakayama Relay Station|qq=}}
{{ill|Mount Daidenji|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Daidenji|qq=}} is a mountain with {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Kofun Group|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Kofun Group|qq=}}
'''

On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Middle Ages|qq=}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|qq=}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|ja|伊達綱村|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Tsunamura|qq=}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|qq=}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku sect|ja|黄檗宗|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōbaku sect|qq=}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|qq=}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|qq=}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji era|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji era|qq=}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haibutsu kishaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Haibutsu kishaku|qq=}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōwa era|qq=}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|qq=}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|ja|宮城テレビ放送|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyagi Television Broadcasting|qq=}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai|ja|NHK仙台放送局|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/NHK Sendai|qq=}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting|ja|東北放送|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Broadcasting|qq=}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|ja|東日本放送|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashinippon Broadcasting|qq=}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Broadcasting|ja|仙台放送|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Broadcasting|qq=}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|qq=}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|qq=}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|qq=}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|qq=}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|qq=}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|qq=}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|qq=}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|qq=}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|qq=}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|qq=}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|qq=}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>
== See Also == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Television Relay Stations|qq=}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/New World Nakayama Relay Station|qq=}}
{{ill|Mount Daidenji|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Daidenji|qq=}} is a mountain with {{ill|Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Kofun Group|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daidenjiyama Yokonahaka Kofun Group|qq=}}

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|qq=}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|qq=}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|qq=}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|qq=}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|qq=}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|qq=}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|qq=}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|qq=}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|qq=}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|qq=}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>

On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). == History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|qq=}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|qq=}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|qq=}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|qq=}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|qq=}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|qq=}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[mountain]] located in [[Taihaku-ku]], [[Sendai]], [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|qq=}}, a [[Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|qq=}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[elevation]] is approximately 120 [[meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|qq=}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|qq=}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|qq=}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|qq=}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|qq=}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|qq=}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|qq=}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|qq=}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|qq=}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|qq=}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
