<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11435319]] Wikidata name: Mount Dainenji [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:19, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[:en:Mountain|Mountain]] located in [[:en:Taihaku-ku|Taihaku-ku]], [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], [[:en:Miyagi Prefecture|Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|1=Dainen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435318}}, a [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|1=Sendai Wild Plants Garden|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q9010989}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[:en:Elevation|Elevation]] is approximately 120 [[:en:Meters|Meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>
== See Also == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Television Relay Stations|1=Sendai City Television Relay Stations|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11377839}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/New World Nakayama Relay Station|1=New World Nakayama Relay Station|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11325002}}

== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11435319]] Wikidata name: Mount Dainenji [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:19, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[:en:Mountain|Mountain]] located in [[:en:Taihaku-ku|Taihaku-ku]], [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], [[:en:Miyagi Prefecture|Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|1=Dainen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435318}}, a [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|1=Sendai Wild Plants Garden|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q9010989}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[:en:Elevation|Elevation]] is approximately 120 [[:en:Meters|Meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11435319]] Wikidata name: Mount Dainenji [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:19, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[:en:Mountain|Mountain]] located in [[:en:Taihaku-ku|Taihaku-ku]], [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], [[:en:Miyagi Prefecture|Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|1=Dainen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435318}}, a [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|1=Sendai Wild Plants Garden|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q9010989}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[:en:Elevation|Elevation]] is approximately 120 [[:en:Meters|Meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11435319]] Wikidata name: Mount Dainenji [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:19, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a [[:en:Mountain|Mountain]] located in [[:en:Taihaku-ku|Taihaku-ku]], [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], [[:en:Miyagi Prefecture|Miyagi Prefecture]]. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|1=Dainen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435318}}, a [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku]] sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|1=Sendai Wild Plants Garden|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q9010989}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The [[:en:Elevation|Elevation]] is approximately 120 [[:en:Meters|Meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order [[:en:Triangulation station|Triangulation point]] "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]], many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the [[:en:Middle Ages|Middle Ages]], the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), [[:en:Date Tsunamura|Date Tsunamura]] began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the [[:en:Ōbaku|Ōbaku sect]] monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and the [[:en:Haibutsu kishaku|Haibutsu kishaku]] movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]], relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * [[:en:Miyagi Television Broadcasting|Miyagi Television Broadcasting]] (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of [[:en:NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|NHK Sendai]], [[:en:Tohoku Broadcasting Company|Tohoku Broadcasting]] (TBC), and [[:en:Higashinippon Broadcasting|Higashinippon Broadcasting]] (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * [[:en:Sendai Television|Sendai Broadcasting]] (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
== References == <references/>
== See Also == * {{ill|Sendai City Television Relay Stations|ja|仙台市内テレビ中継局|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Television Relay Stations|1=Sendai City Television Relay Stations|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11377839}} * {{ill|New World Nakayama Relay Station|ja|ニューワールド中山中継局|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/New World Nakayama Relay Station|1=New World Nakayama Relay Station|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11325002}}

The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|1=Dainen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435318}}, a {{ill|Ōbaku|en|Ōbaku|WD=Q384728|lt=Ōbaku}} sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|1=Sendai Wild Plants Garden|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q9010989}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The {{ill|Elevation|en|Elevation|WD=Q2633778|lt=Elevation}} is approximately 120 [[:en:Meters|Meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation station|en|Triangulation station|WD=Q131862|lt=Triangulation point}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|WD=Q12554|lt=Middle Ages}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|en|Date Tsunamura|WD=Q5227557|lt=Date Tsunamura}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku|en|Ōbaku|WD=Q384728|lt=Ōbaku sect}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|en|Haibutsu kishaku|WD=Q702298|lt=Haibutsu kishaku}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|en|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|WD=Q3082642|lt=Miyagi Television Broadcasting}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|en|NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|WD=Q2272909|lt=NHK Sendai}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting Company|en|Tohoku Broadcasting Company|WD=Q843723|lt=Tohoku Broadcasting}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|en|Higashinippon Broadcasting|WD=Q843355|lt=Higashinippon Broadcasting}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Television|en|Sendai Television|WD=Q843347|lt=Sendai Broadcasting}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|1=Dainen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435318}}, a {{ill|Ōbaku|en|Ōbaku|WD=Q384728|lt=Ōbaku}} sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|1=Sendai Wild Plants Garden|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q9010989}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The {{ill|Elevation|en|Elevation|WD=Q2633778|lt=Elevation}} is approximately 120 [[:en:Meters|Meters]].

== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation station|en|Triangulation station|WD=Q131862|lt=Triangulation point}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|WD=Q12554|lt=Middle Ages}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|en|Date Tsunamura|WD=Q5227557|lt=Date Tsunamura}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku|en|Ōbaku|WD=Q384728|lt=Ōbaku sect}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|en|Haibutsu kishaku|WD=Q702298|lt=Haibutsu kishaku}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|en|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|WD=Q3082642|lt=Miyagi Television Broadcasting}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|en|NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|WD=Q2272909|lt=NHK Sendai}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting Company|en|Tohoku Broadcasting Company|WD=Q843723|lt=Tohoku Broadcasting}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|en|Higashinippon Broadcasting|WD=Q843355|lt=Higashinippon Broadcasting}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Television|en|Sendai Television|WD=Q843347|lt=Sendai Broadcasting}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Dainenjiyama]][[ja:大年寺山]][[lld:Mont Dainenji]]
{{Coord|38|14|16.7|N|140|52|40.3|E|display=title}}'''Dainenjiyama''' (大年寺山) is a {{ill|Mountain|en|Mountain|WD=Q8502|lt=Mountain}} located in [[:en:Taihaku-ku|Taihaku-ku]], {{ill|Sendai|en|Sendai|WD=Q46747|lt=Sendai}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|en|Miyagi Prefecture|WD=Q47896|lt=Miyagi Prefecture}}. The name of the mountain derives from {{ill|Dainenji|ja|大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji|1=Dainen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435318}}, a {{ill|Ōbaku|en|Ōbaku|WD=Q384728|lt=Ōbaku}} sect temple that has stood on the mountain since the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. In earlier times, the mountain was known as '''Noguchi-yama''' or '''Mogasaki'''. The area features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and part of the park houses the {{ill|Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|ja|仙台市野草園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai City Wild Grass Garden|1=Sendai Wild Plants Garden|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q9010989}}. Additionally, three television towers belonging to broadcasting stations stand on the mountain. The {{ill|Elevation|en|Elevation|WD=Q2633778|lt=Elevation}} is approximately 120 [[:en:Meters|Meters]].
{{GeoGroup}} [[File:DainenTempleMainGate2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Dainenji Main Gate (November 2007)]] [[File:DainenjiDateTomb2007-11-14.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Date Clan Cemetery (November 2007)]]
== Geography == Dainenjiyama is located south of [[downtown Sendai]], separated by the {{ill|Hirose River (Miyagi)|ja|広瀬川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose River (Miyagi)|1=Hirose River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485580}} and {{ill|Atagoyama (Sendai)|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama (Sendai)|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}}, along with the Okubo Marsh. The Nagamachi district stretches out to the south of the mountain.
The shape of the mountain extends from east-northeast to west-southwest. The highest point of the mountain was historically recorded as the second-order {{ill|Triangulation station|en|Triangulation station|WD=Q131862|lt=Triangulation point}} "Dainenji" ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|25|E|region:JP|name=Former Second-Order Triangulation Point "Dainenji"}}) with an elevation of 119.55 meters, but this point has since been decommissioned (relocated).
On the southwestern slope is the {{ill|Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学長町キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamachi Campus of Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|4.6|N|140|52|26.5|E|region:JP|name=Tohoku Institute of Technology Nagamachi Campus}}). On the northwestern slope is the Sendai City Wild Grass Garden ({{Coord|38|14|19.7|N|140|52|25.7|E|region:JP|name=Sendai City Wild Grass Garden}}), while the eastern side features {{ill|Dainenji Park|ja|大年寺公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenji Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including the {{ill|Date Clan Cemetery|ja|伊達家の墓所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Clan Cemetery|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{Coord|38|14|25.9|N|140|52|46.8|E|region:JP|name=Date Clan Cemetery}}). The northeastern foot of the mountain is close to the Hirose River.
== History == During the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, many {{ill|Yokoana tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana tombs|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave tomb|qq=}} were built on the mountain’s slopes. The north side contains the {{ill|Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainenjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while the south side has the {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}, with additional clusters such as the {{ill|Atagoyama Cave Tombs|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Cave Tombs|qq=}} and {{ill|Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōzenji Cave Tomb Cluster|qq=}}. Collectively, these sites are known as the {{ill|Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>[http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/k0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] (Sendai City Board of Education)</ref>
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|WD=Q12554|lt=Middle Ages}}, the mountain was called Mogasaki and was the site of {{ill|Mogasaki Castle|ja|茂ヶ崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mogasaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
In 1696 (Genroku 9), {{ill|Date Tsunamura|en|Date Tsunamura|WD=Q5227557|lt=Date Tsunamura}} began the construction of a grand temple complex on Mogasaki, relocating and reconstructing the abandoned {{ill|Sen'ei-ji|ja|仙英寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sen'ei-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The following year, the {{ill|Ōbaku|en|Ōbaku|WD=Q384728|lt=Ōbaku sect}} monk {{ill|Tetsugyu|ja|鉄牛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsugyu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鉄牛道機|1=Tetsugyū Dōki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1713450}} was invited to establish {{ill|Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja|両足山大年寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryōsokuzan Dainenji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. From this time onward, it served as the burial site for successive generations of the Date Clan (except those who passed away in Edo). Dainenji flourished under the patronage of the Date family and became one of the largest Ōbaku temples in Japan. However, during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} and the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|en|Haibutsu kishaku|WD=Q702298|lt=Haibutsu kishaku}} movement, the Date family abandoned Buddhist rites, leading to the temple’s decline. Today, the only remaining original structure is the Main Gate ({{Coord|38|14|13.1|N|140|52|44.3|E|region:JP|name=Former Dainenji Main Gate}}).
In 1918 (Taishō 7), more than 60 laborers barricaded themselves on Dainenjiyama during a labor dispute at a local factory. This early labor movement protest led to a successful wage increase.
The Ōbaku sect later rebuilt Dainenji in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}}, relocating it to the foot of the mountain ({{Coord|38|14|13.4|N|140|52|46.7|E|region:JP|name=Current Dainenji}}).
In 1934 (Shōwa 9), along with neighboring {{ill|Yagiyama|ja|八木山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagiyama|1=Yagiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q28688586}}, a total of 308.32 hectares were designated as "Yagiyama Dainenjiyama Scenic Area" to preserve the green space near Sendai.<ref>Sendai City History, Volume 2 (1955).</ref>
== Television Towers == {{GeoGroup|section=Television Towers}} [[File:Mt._Dainenji_seen_from_the_SS30.jpg|thumb|260px|right|Television towers on Dainenjiyama]] The most striking feature of Dainenjiyama is the presence of three television towers. From east to west: * {{ill|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|en|Miyagi Television Broadcasting|WD=Q3082642|lt=Miyagi Television Broadcasting}} (MMT) ({{Coord|38|14|24.8|N|140|52|41|E|region:JP|name=Miyagi Television Tower}}) * Joint tower of {{ill|NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|en|NHK Sendai Broadcasting Station|WD=Q2272909|lt=NHK Sendai}}, {{ill|Tohoku Broadcasting Company|en|Tohoku Broadcasting Company|WD=Q843723|lt=Tohoku Broadcasting}} (TBC), and {{ill|Higashinippon Broadcasting|en|Higashinippon Broadcasting|WD=Q843355|lt=Higashinippon Broadcasting}} (KHB) ({{Coord|38|14|18.5|N|140|52|27.5|E|region:JP|name=NHK Sendai and others Tower}}) * {{ill|Sendai Television|en|Sendai Television|WD=Q843347|lt=Sendai Broadcasting}} (OX) and {{ill|FM Sendai|ja|エフエム仙台|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/FM Sendai|1=FM Sendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10854520}} shared tower ({{Coord|38|14|15|N|140|52|22.6|E|region:JP|name=Sendai Broadcasting Tower}})
